items.title: Edgar "Sambo" Joseph Interview, 1960-08-07
items.q: one time we played, John would tell you it was John Woodnette. I played for a bunch of white soldiers over the river.

ctx.x: That's the terrible thing. Well, did you ever play, you know, these funerals? I noticed these funerals, they play when they're reading the music. That'd be kind of tough to be walking and reading music too, wouldn't it?

No, it's not. No, it's not. Your breath, your breath, you have it up high. You don't be playing all that, you don't play. Them numbers most, they, they, you see what they're telling them? Them fellas don't be playing what's on that. They knows them numbers. They have it up there, but they don't be watching that. They knows it, they knows it. They know it. A man pick up a hymn, like Maryamagod the D, what friend we have in Jesus, they know you play it. All right, you know you know it. You know what key is written…
Man, you know them colored soldiers and white soldiers be right up on top of us? Yeah, I know, they can really step out of us. Man, they can walk, they can walk. They can walk.
